decided_by: team (user choice), before any model tuning
score: P(enjoyed) from a gradient-boosted classifier (sklearn HistGradientBoosting, 400 iters, lr 0.05, 31 leaves, l2 1.0)

features.g: percentile of the user's playtime among that game's players
features.resid: log1p(playtime) minus user + game effects (two-way fixed effects, shrinkage 5, 8 sweeps)
features.u_rank: percentile of the game's playtime inside the user's own library

training_target: review flag (noisy label), report/calibration split by user_key % 2; Kaggle bulk reviewers excluded
fit_on: training split only; one model per dataset (pooling and monotonic constraints tested: no gain)
graded_relevance: use the probability directly; ALS confidence c = 1 + alpha * P(enjoyed)
binary_cutoff: maximize kappa on calibration users of the training split; computed in the model pipeline
rows_used: played > 0 and history_ok; zero playtime stays unknown

results_report_users.note: within-user AUC is inflated by game quality (quality-only score: 0.747 on Kaggle); within-game AUC is the clean metric

previous_label.rule: enjoyed = playtime >= 2 h, or > 0 h when the game's training-median playtime is under 3 h
previous_label.why: Same label for both datasets. Wins on McAuley, the primary training data (kappa 0.221 vs 0.134 for the two-sided label); on Kaggle it scores 0.202 vs 0.256 for the two-sided label.

status: superseded for production by the 2026-10-30 re-test: use game-relative playtime percentile (g, playtime now); two-stage kept as research only

stage2.model: gradient boosting (200 iters, lr 0.05, 7 leaves, min 50 per leaf, l2 1.0)
stage2.fallback: no achievement data -> has_ach = 0 and the model scores from stage 1 alone
stage2.code: label/achievements.py, label/tune_stage2.py, label/holdout_eval.py; model in label/cache/enjoy_two_stage.pkl

stage1_tuned.why: tuning +0.017 AUC; Kaggle-trained versions transfer poorly to McAuley-style players (0.59–0.65); 3 extra features added nothing

fresh_retest_2026_10_30.data: Steam IUserReviewsService, 94,878 'all recent' reviews over 922 games; 2,276 reviewers with public libraries (one review each)
fresh_retest_2026_10_30.refit_cv: refitting on fresh data did not beat raw playtime (g + resid 0.717 vs 0.725 within-game, 47 games, noisy)
artifacts_found: negative-review page reaches further back in time -> recency features leaked review age
650 prolific reviewers dominated library-linked rows -> library size leaked reviewer type
previous '2-hour floor' baseline used playtime tie-breaks, so it ranked exactly like raw playtime
fresh_retest_2026_10_30.decision: enjoyed score = percentile of the user's lifetime playtime among the game's players (g); 2-hour floor as a hard minimum only for binary labels
